name: セアブラノ神 伏見剛力 (Seabura no Kami Fushimi Goriki)

claims.text: A dedicated Jiro-style ramen kitchen using wheat noodles and wheat soy-sauce tare in a small shared space; no gluten-free preparation and high risk of wheat throughout.
The back fat and tare are seasoned with Kyoto Gokko (五光) soy sauce, a standard wheat-containing shoyu.
Broth is pork-bone and fish based with back fat and pork toppings; even vegetable items are served in the meat/fish broth, so no dish is free of animal products.

name: せんぼんぐらばー館 (Senbon Gurabaa-kan)

claims.text: Wheat is central throughout: champon and sara-udon are wheat noodles, dumplings have wheat skins, and a single shared wok and fryer handle all dishes, so cross-contact with wheat is unavoidable in a kitchen this size.
As a Japanese town-Chinese kitchen, dishes are seasoned with standard soy sauce and the gravy/seasonings expected to contain wheat; no wheat-free soy alternative is indicated.
Broths and stir-fries are built on pork and seafood, and the wok is shared across all orders, so any 'vegetable' dish would still carry animal-derived broth and cross-contact.

name: 新宿めんや風花 (Shinjuku Menya Fuhka)

claims.text: Every bowl is built on hand-kneaded wheat noodles; no gluten-free option or allergen handling is documented.
Chashu and some bowls carry a soy-sauce element typical of ramen, which is normally wheat-based; no wheat-free tare is mentioned.
Broths are animal- and seafood-based (chicken/duck plus seafood and vegetable stocks) and bowls are topped with chashu pork; no separate vegan preparation exists.

name: 新福菜館 本店 (Shinpuku Saikan Honten)

claims.text: The core dish is wheat ramen noodles, so wheat is present and boiled in shared water; no gluten-free preparation exists.
The signature black broth is built on a soy-sauce tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, making the broth itself unsafe for celiac diners.
Broth is a pork- and chicken-bone base and chashu (roast pork) is a standard topping; nothing on the menu is vegan or vegetarian.

name: 新進亭 一乗寺店 (Shinshintei Ichijoji)

claims.text: The shop's core product is white miso ramen with wheat noodles and a miso-based tare; miso and the broth components typically contain wheat, and no gluten-free preparation is offered.
Bowls are built on dashi and meat elements with chashu and other meat toppings; no vegan or vegetarian broth is offered.

A back-fat shoyu ramen shop with a single shared workflow (one pot of wheat noodles, shared utensils, soy-based tare); cross-contact with wheat is effectively unavoidable for a gluten-sensitive diner.
The bowl is a soy-sauce (shoyu) ramen; Japanese soy sauce used for ramen tare almost always contains wheat, and no wheat-free tare is documented here.
The broth itself is animal-based (pork/chicken bone with back fat), so even non-meat menu items would share an animal-stock kitchen; no vegan-safe preparation is documented.
All bowls use straight wheat noodles sourced from a noodle factory; there is no gluten-free noodle and the entire menu is wheat-based.
The dishes are Sichuan-style tantanmen and mapo, which conventionally use wheat-based soy sauce in the tare and sauces; no wheat-free soy sauce is indicated.
Every dish uses sweet ground pork and Chinese-style meat broth, including the tantanmen, soupless tantanmen, and mapo tofu/rice; no plant-based option exists.
Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in the shared pot used for all ramen; no gluten-free preparation exists.
The signature ramen is a fish-infused soy-sauce (shoyu) flavor; Japanese shoyu tare is wheat-based, so the broth itself contains wheat.
Broths are animal-based (pork bone, chicken carcass and dried-fish dashi); no separate plant-based stock is used.
